newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Devaluation of Vietnam dong not planned - minister.
newsitem.headline: Devaluation of Vietnam dong not planned - minister.

text.p: Vietnam's new finance minister, Nguyen Sinh Hung, said on Monday that a devaluation of the Vietnamese dong was not being planned.
Hung told reporters during a break in National Assembly proceedings that the authorities wanted to manage the dong, ensuring "reasonably stable" rates against other currencies.
"The Vietnamese government or the (central) bank have never mentioned the possibility of devaluing the Vietnamese currency," Hung said. "That's why I don't think it's an issue to be discussed.
"What we will try to do is regulate the rate ... of the Vietnamese currency with other currencies," he added.
The central State Bank of Vietnam moved last month to dampen speculation of an imminent devaluation to tackle a fast-growing trade deficit.
The dong has been steady at around 11,000 per dollar since 1994. It was quoted at 11,075 on Monday.

Bankers and economists have said that a cut in the value of the dong could help narrow the country's trade gap. The Trade Ministry said at the weekend that it expected the deficit to jump to a record $4.0 billion this year from $2.3 billion in 1995.
